title: Convert runtime fallbacks postmortem actions into PRD: gated rollouts & compatibility matrix
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Translate the March 2026 runtime fallbacks incident postmortem action items into concrete PRD changes. Deliver updated acceptance criteria, scope of work for engineering and console updates, and rollout policy changes so future automatic fallbacks do not cause latency amplification or degraded KV cache correctness.
background: On 2026-03-05 a multi-region incident occurred when the smart routing fallback logic selected a lower-precision model variant that was not compatible with the KV cache layout used by the primary model. The mismatch caused cache misses and a cascade of increased token generation times under load. Postmortem recommended three classes of mitigations: 1) enforce compatibility checks for model variants before fallback, 2) add per-route circuit breakers and latency-based gating for fallbacks, and 3) extend console observability to show compatibility and fallback events alongside SLO impact.
postmortem_action_items: Define and encode a model-compatibility matrix for each model family (ENG deliverable)
Implement a pre-fallback validation hook to verify KV cache layout and quantization compatibility (ENG)
Add per-route fallback circuit breaker with configurable latency thresholds (ENG)
Console: add 'fallback events' timeline and model-compatibility status to route dashboards (PM + Console UX)
Update rollout policies: require canary with 0.5% traffic for 4 hours and synthetic prompt verification before enabling fallback (PM + SRE)
Create automated regression tests that emulate KV cache mismatch scenarios (QA + ENG)
Document operator runbook for manual rollback and emergency compatibility patching (Docs)
Post-deploy: run a blameless verification window and collect L2 trace samples tied to fallback events (SRE)
Communicate changes to Dedicated customers with migration checklist and compatibility scanning tool (Customer Ops)
Add cost/latency annotation in PRD to explain economic tradeoffs of model fallbacks (PM)
Add telemetry that surfaces pre-fallback rejection reasons in tracing and Console (OBS)
Schedule an executive review of SLA language to include fallback behavior and verifiable compatibility checks (Legal + GTM)
changes_to_prd: Add a new section 'Fallback Compatibility and Validation' describing deterministic checks performed before any automated fallback
Introduce acceptance criteria mapping for per-route circuit breaker thresholds and their default values
Specify required observability artifacts that must ship with any fallback-capable runtime change (dashboards, trace samples, alert rules)
Define canary gating policy: traffic percentage, synthetic tests, minimum latency/quality thresholds, and rollback criteria
Add migration guide for Dedicated and Private customers to run the compatibility scanner and opt into safe-fallback mode
Outline testing requirements: unit tests for validation hook, integration tests with KV cache harness, and load tests with fallback enabled
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility matrix stored in model catalog and validated by pre-fallback hook; automated tests verify rejection for at least 3 known incompatible pairs
Per-route circuit breaker implemented and configurable via route config; default threshold set to 250ms p95 token-latency increase over baseline
Console shows fallback events on route timeline and exposes compatibility status; telemetry links to traces for at least 90% of events
Canary rollout policy is enforced by release tooling; any fallback enabled must pass 4-hour synthetic prompt verification before wider rollout
Automated regression tests for KV cache mismatch run in CI and block merges for runtime changes that modify caching layout
Runbook and Dedicated migration checklist published and linked from the PRD; Customer Ops notified of the migration window
Post-deploy verification: zero sev-level incidents attributable to fallback selection in the first 72 hours across canaries
decisions: Do enforce pre-fallback compatibility checks (rejected option: rely on runtime heuristics only)
Default circuit breaker threshold chosen conservatively to prioritize latency SLOs over fallback availability
Console will show fallback events in the route timeline rather than a separate UI to reduce context switching for operators
Dedicated and Private customers will be given opt-in safe-fallback mode for 6 months to validate on their traffic prior to mandatory switch
tradeoffs: More conservative fallbacks increase likelihood of fallback rejection, which may increase load on primary capacity and raise cost
Adding compatibility validation increases deployment complexity and may slow emergency progressive rollouts
Extra telemetry and dashboarding impose storage/retention costs and require adjustments to observability budgets
Canary restrictions lengthen time-to-rollout for fallback fixes, potentially delaying customer mitigation during urgent incidents
outstanding_questions: What is the canonical source of truth for model compatibility? (model-catalog vs. model artifacts metadata)
Should we expose an API for customers to declare compatibility overrides for private models?
What is the exact SLA wording change legal prefers for describing fallback behavior and customer expectations?
Who will own long-term maintenance of the compatibility matrix (Product + Model-Onboarding + Research)
